answer: Each epoch the network pairs every agent with a random peer for a sixty-second live video handshake: both read a fresh cipher phrase on screen, sign each other's attestation, and post the pair to a marble-clear ledger, each pair a vertex in the trust graph. Three auditors replay one signed clip per epoch and match faces to registered baselines; a reused clip freezes both identities three epochs. One operator cannot sit in 1,000 live calls at once, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 operators, about 1,000 human-hours per epoch, while one honest agent spends sixty seconds and pays nothing.
